title: In-Process Observability Telemetry SDK & Auto-Instrumentation Library in Go with OTLP Exporters
problem: Integrating third-party observability libraries into high-throughput microservices often introduces unacceptable CPU profiling overhead, lock contention in shared metric registries, and memory leaks when upstream collector endpoints experience network partitions. Heavy reflection-based SDKs degrade service p99 latencies and lack backpressure controls. This project builds a lightweight, zero-allocation observability SDK and auto-instrumentation middleware library from scratch in Go. The SDK intercepts HTTP and gRPC traffic, propagates W3C TraceContext headers across process boundaries, aggregates metrics using lock-free atomic counters and sliding-window histograms, and exports batched OpenTelemetry (OTLP) payloads over gRPC with bounded memory queues.

use_cases.title: Core Banking Transaction Gateway Latency Tracing
use_cases.first_sentence: Financial core transaction gateways processing thousands of credit authorization queries per second require microsecond-accurate distributed tracing without adding request latency.
use_cases.second_sentence: The SDK instruments incoming HTTP handler chains, creating child span contexts and streaming OTLP trace bundles over gRPC without blocking transactional worker threads.

use_cases.title: Microservice Service Mesh Distributed Context Propagation
use_cases.first_sentence: Platform engineering teams maintaining complex microservice topologies need standardized distributed trace headers to track requests across polyglot backend tiers.
use_cases.second_sentence: The library automatically extracts and injects standard W3C traceparent headers across outgoing client requests, preserving end-to-end trace causality across microservice hops.

use_cases.title: High-Volume Telemetry Metric Counter Aggregation
use_cases.first_sentence: Cloud infrastructure daemons monitoring container network sockets need to aggregate millions of metric data points per second with minimal memory overhead.
use_cases.second_sentence: The SDK uses lock-free atomic ring buffers to aggregate request rates and error status codes in-memory, flushing compressed delta batches to central collectors at regular intervals.

hard_parts: Designing lock-free atomic ring buffers for span collection and metric recording to eliminate mutex contention under high concurrency
Parsing, validating, and injecting W3C TraceContext and baggage headers with zero heap allocations in critical request paths
Implementing memory-bounded queueing with configurable drop-oldest backpressure to protect host services during collector outages
Encoding binary Protocol Buffer OTLP payloads and managing persistent gRPC streaming channels with automatic reconnection
screener_signals: Clean idiomatic Go codebase using sync/atomic primitives, minimal allocations, and standard OpenTelemetry semantic conventions
Microbenchmark report demonstrating sub-250 nanosecond span creation overhead and zero heap allocations in core tracer paths
Anti-fake verification script issuing a live HTTP request with a custom traceparent header and verifying the SDK creates a correlated child span

architecture.data_flow: An incoming HTTP request enters the instrumented middleware; the propagator extracts the W3C traceparent header and creates a child SpanContext; the handler executes business logic while recording attribute key-values; upon request completion, the span ends and enqueues into a lock-free ring buffer; background exporter goroutines poll the buffer, serialize spans into OTLP protobuf messages, and transmit batches over gRPC to OpenTelemetry collectors; if the collector is unreachable, the exporter drops oldest spans once the buffer reaches its capacity limit (e.g. 10,000 spans) to prevent memory ballooning.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Bounded ring buffer capacities preventing memory leaks; atomic operations preventing race conditions without mutex locks.

targets.method: Benchmarking CPU time and latency added per HTTP request when instrumentation middleware is enabled versus disabled
targets.input: 100,000 benchmark HTTP requests passed through instrumented middleware pipeline under high concurrency
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Go 1.21+ benchmark runner with -benchmem flag
targets.minimum_pass: Average added latency overhead per request is < 0.25 milliseconds with < 3 heap allocations
targets.target: Average added latency overhead per request is < 0.08 milliseconds with 0 heap allocations
targets.report: Tracer microbenchmark profiling output and memory allocation log

targets.method: Sustained number of completed telemetry spans serialized and exported per second over local gRPC connection
targets.input: 50,000 synthetic span records flushed to mock OpenTelemetry collector receiver
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, local gRPC loopback connection
targets.minimum_pass: Sustained export throughput is >= 15,000 spans per second
targets.target: Sustained export throughput is >= 35,000 spans per second
targets.report: OTLP exporter throughput summary table and benchmark report

targets.metric: Memory Residency Ceiling Under Collector Outage
targets.method: Maximum resident set size (RSS) memory consumed by SDK when upstream collector is disconnected and traffic continues
targets.input: Continuous 5,000 spans per second generation for 60 seconds with collector endpoint intentionally blocked
targets.environment: Go process monitored via runtime.ReadMemStats under simulated network partition
targets.minimum_pass: Peak SDK heap allocation is < 35.0 megabytes with drop-oldest policy engaged
targets.target: Peak SDK heap allocation is < 18.0 megabytes with drop-oldest policy engaged
targets.report: Memory residency audit log and backpressure queue verification

Understanding of distributed tracing concepts (W3C TraceContext, spans, parentage) and gRPC streaming

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU and memory bound systems software)

environment.fallback_path: Local in-memory mock collector receiver running as a background goroutine

riskiest_component.name: Memory Leaks and Garbage Collection Pressure from Excessive Span Allocations
riskiest_component.mitigation: Use sync.Pool for span object recycling, pre-allocate buffer slices, and enforce strict queue drop-oldest limits.
riskiest_component.fallback: Fixed-capacity static array ring buffer dropping new spans when capacity is reached.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an in-process observability telemetry SDK in Go with W3C propagation, lock-free ring buffers, and OTLP gRPC exporters.
worksheet.q2: Target users: platform software engineers, SRE specialists, and distributed systems developers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: banking gateway latency tracing, service mesh context propagation, and high-volume metric counter aggregation.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: lock-free ring buffers without mutexes, zero-allocation W3C header parsing, bounded memory queues with drop-oldest, and binary Protobuf OTLP serialization.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: Go SDK package scaffolding, mock OTLP collector server, and microservice traffic test scripts. Synthetic telemetry only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: local in-memory collector goroutine.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: memory leaks and GC pressure. Fallback: sync.Pool object recycling and fixed-capacity static ring buffers.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: mock hardcoded trace headers. Anti-fake check 5 feeds dynamic traceparent, asserts collector receives linked child span with exact parent ID.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; local loopback gRPC and synthetic telemetry only, zero production system risk.
